newsitem.title: USA: Canada hopes for successful euro, says first year key.
newsitem.headline: Canada hopes for successful euro, says first year key.

text.p: Canada is keen to see a successful launch of the planned single European currency, and will be looking closely at how well the currency establishes itself in the first year, senior Canadian government officials said on Friday.

The officials were briefing journalists at the G7 summit meeting in Denver on meetings between Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and European Union officials, including Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and European Commission president Jacques Santer.

One official said there had been "no discussion of the euro per se" in the meetings, but that Kok had informed Chretien of discussions earlier this week in the Dutch capital of Amsterdam, where European Union nations agreed a new treaty.
"It is clear that this is the most important item on the agenda (for Europe)," the source said.

Asked about Canada's policy and level of interest in the launch of the new currency, set for 1999, the official said, "It is simple. We want a successful euro because we don't want them to screw up the financial markets.
"(A successful euro) will be good for investments and exports. If it is not a good euro then that is another matter."

The official, noting that while the press in some countries in Europe seemed to be sceptical of the prospects for a timely launch of the euro the European Commission itself was confident of a punctual start, said that Canada would be looking closely at the currency's first year of existence.
A successful start could prompt Britain to join the currency group, he added.
"January 1999 is not the end of the story, it is just the beginning of the process. It will be interesting to see how it will go in the first year," the Canadian official said.
"If it is going well then our British friends, who have been sitting on the fence, may decide to join the group."
